So far, the only filters for site/fire selection have been selecting for fires withing the past ~15 years (2010-2024) which intersect with previous fuels reduction. Now we will impose 2 more filters:
-- Treatment Extent: The proportion of the wildfire treated must be equal to or greater than 0.1, when rounded to two decimal points. This is to improve site sampling within each fire. The proportion treated must be lower than 98% to allow for selection of controls.
-- Elevation: The minimum elevation of the fire must be greater than 1500 m. This is to exclude lower-elevation vegetation types.

```{r}
#load packages
library(sf) 
library(terra)
library(tidyverse)
```

# Load My GeoPackage

```{r}
intersection <- st_read("data/processed/fuels_analysis.gpkg", layer = "intersection")
fires <- st_read("data/processed/fuels_analysis.gpkg", layer = "fires")
treatments <- st_read("data/processed/fuels_analysis.gpkg", layer = "treatments")
```

# Find Values for Each Fire

## Treatment Extent

```{r}
# Calculate the unique (flat) treated area in each fire (in hectares)
treated_area_df <- intersection %>%
  group_by(Event_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    geometry = st_union(geom),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    unique_treated_area_ha = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 10000) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() 

# Calculate the total fire area (in hectares)
fires_area_df <- fires %>%
  mutate(
    total_fire_area_ha = as.numeric(st_area(geom)) / 10000) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>% # Drop geometry
  dplyr::select(Event_ID, total_fire_area_ha)

# Join the two datasets and calculate proportion
extent_df <- fires_area_df %>%
  left_join(treated_area_df, by = "Event_ID") %>%
  mutate(
    Proportion_Treated = unique_treated_area_ha / total_fire_area_ha,
    Fire_Area_ha = total_fire_area_ha) %>%
  select(Event_ID, Fire_Area_ha, Proportion_Treated)
```

## Elevation
```{r}
# Load the elevation raster
elevation_rast <- rast("D:/Spatial_Data/LANDFIRE/LF2020_Elev_CONUS/Tif/LF2020_Elev_CONUS.tif")

# Function to find elevation range of each fire
get_elevation_range <- function(geometry, raster) {
  
  # Convert the sf geometry object to a SpatVector
  spat_vector <- terra::vect(geometry) 
  
  # Use terra's extract function with the SpatVector
  # By setting fun = NULL, we get all values, then calculate min/max manually.
  values <- terra::extract(raster, spat_vector, fun = NULL, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Check if any non-NA values were extracted
  if (is.null(values) || all(is.na(values[, 2]))) {
    return(c(min_elev = NA, max_elev = NA))
  }
  
  # The second column contains the elevation values (column 1 is the ID)
  elev_values <- values[, 2] 
  
  # Calculate range
  min_val <- min(elev_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(elev_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  return(c(min_elev = min_val, max_elev = max_val))
}

# Main Processing Loop
fire_names <- unique(fires$Event_ID)
results_list <- list()

for (name in fire_names) {
  
  # --- Filter Data for the Current Fire ---
  
  # Get the total area geometry for the current fire (Union geometries if multiple parts exist)
  fire_geom <- fires %>%
    filter(Event_ID == name) %>%
    st_union()
  
  # Get the treated area geometry for the current fire
  treatment_geom <- intersection %>%
    filter(Event_ID == name) %>%
    st_union()
  
  # --- Calculate Elevation Ranges ---
  
  # a) Fire Range
  fire_range <- get_elevation_range(fire_geom, elevation_rast)
  
  # b) Treatment Range
  treatment_range <- get_elevation_range(treatment_geom, elevation_rast)
  
  # --- Compile Results ---
  results_list[[name]] <- data.frame(
    Event_ID = name,
    Fire_Min_Elev = fire_range["min_elev"],
    Fire_Max_Elev = fire_range["max_elev"],
    Treatment_Min_Elev = treatment_range["min_elev"],
    Treatment_Max_Elev = treatment_range["max_elev"]
  )
}

# Create Table
elev_table <- do.call(rbind, results_list) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "ID") %>% # Clean up row names
  dplyr::select(-ID)
```

## Join Dataframes

```{r}
# Merge the Dataframes
char_table <- fires %>%
  inner_join(extent_df, by = "Event_ID") %>%
  inner_join(elev_table, by = "Event_ID") %>%
  mutate(
    Fire_Min_Elev = as.integer(Fire_Min_Elev),
    Fire_Max_Elev = as.integer(Fire_Max_Elev),
    Treatment_Min_Elev = as.integer(Treatment_Min_Elev),
    Treatment_Max_Elev = as.integer(Treatment_Max_Elev),
    Fire_Area_ha = round(Fire_Area_ha, digits = 0),
    Proportion_Treated = round(Proportion_Treated, digits = 2),
  ) %>%
  select(-Ig_Date) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()
```

# Filter Fires

Based on Treatment extent and Elevation

```{r}
myfires <- char_table %>%
  filter(Proportion_Treated >= 0.1) %>% #removed 56 fires
  filter(Proportion_Treated < 0.98) %>% #removed 7 entries
  filter(Fire_Min_Elev > 1500) %>% #removed 9 fires 
  st_drop_geometry()

#View the results
myfires %>%
  group_by(Incid_Name) %>%
  summarise(Proportion_Treated) %>%
  arrange(desc(Proportion_Treated))

write.csv(myfires, "data/processed/my_fires.csv")
```

# Update Geopackage to Reflect Fires Selection

```{r}
myfiresIDs <- myfires$Event_ID

#subset fires
fires_sub <- fires %>% 
  filter(Event_ID %in% myfiresIDs)

#subset the intersection
inter_sub <- intersection %>% 
  filter(Event_ID %in% myfiresIDs)

#subset the treatments
treat_sub <- treatments %>%
  filter(OBJECTID %in% inter_sub$OBJECTID)
```

Save new geopackage

```{r}
# copy over my fires layer
st_write(
  obj = fires_sub,
  dsn = "data/processed/fuels_analysis.gpkg",
  layer = "fires",
  driver = "GPKG",
  delete_dsn = TRUE
)

# copy over my treatments layer
st_write(
  obj = treat_sub,
  dsn = "data/processed/fuels_analysis.gpkg",
  layer = "treatments",
  driver = "GPKG",
  delete_layer= TRUE
)
```

# GEE Shapefile Creation

These shapefiles will be used to create burn severity rasters in Google Earth Engine following Parks methods. 

*Note: Update date in file name when running*

```{r}
## Prepares the selected fires perimeter dataset for use in Sean Parks' GEE code for calculating fire severity
st_read("data/processed/fuels_analysis.gpkg", layer = "fires") %>% # import selected perimeters
  mutate(date = as.Date(Ig_Date), "%Y%m%d") %>% # convert ignition date to date object
  mutate(Start_Day=min(lubridate::yday(date))-14) %>% # set first possible date 
  mutate(End_Day=max(lubridate::yday(date))+14) %>% # set last possible date 
  mutate(Fire_Year=as.character(Fire_Year), Fire_ID=Event_ID) %>% # create variables with column names used in Parks code
  dplyr::select(Fire_ID, Fire_Year, Start_Day, End_Day) %>% # include only Fire ID, Fire Year, Start Day and End Day columns in dataset
  st_write("data/processed/GEE/fires_GEE_1015.shp", delete_dsn = TRUE)


#Do it for treatment fires too
## Prepares the selected fires perimeter dataset for use in Sean Parks' GEE code for calculating fire severity
st_read("data/processed/GEE/treatment_wildfires.shp") %>% # import selected perimeters
  mutate(date = as.Date(Ig_Date), "%Y%m%d") %>% # convert ignition date to date object
  mutate(Start_Day=min(lubridate::yday(date))-14) %>% # set first possible date 
  mutate(End_Day=max(lubridate::yday(date))+14) %>% # set last possible date 
  mutate(Fire_Year= as.character(YEAR_COMP), Fire_ID=Event_ID) %>% # create variables with column names used in Parks code
  dplyr::select(Fire_ID, Fire_Year, Start_Day, End_Day) %>% # include only Fire ID, Fire Year, Start Day and End Day columns in dataset
  st_write("data/processed/GEE/fires_GEE_Treatments_1015.shp", delete_dsn = TRUE)
```
